name: Roquefort
description: A blue-veined sheep's milk cheese aged in the natural limestone caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon. Holds AOP status, which per Marcella the Cheesemonger's guidance requires traditional animal rennet.
tasting_note: Sharp, tangy, and salty with a crumbly texture and a lingering peppery finish from the Penicillium roqueforti veins.

name: Camembert de Normandie
description: Soft, bloomy-rind cow's milk cheese from the village of Camembert. AOP designation requires animal rennet under traditional French cheesemaking rules.
tasting_note: Buttery and mushroomy, runs soft at the rind with a grassy, barnyard depth as it ripens.

name: Brie de Meaux
description: The original AOP Brie from the Meaux region east of Paris, made with raw cow's milk and animal rennet per its protected designation.
tasting_note: Creamy and nutty with a soft edible rind; mellow when young, earthier as it fully ripens.

name: Comté
description: A firm, alpine-style cow's milk cheese from the Jura mountains, aged for months in caves. AOP rules mandate animal rennet.
tasting_note: Nutty and slightly sweet with notes of toasted hazelnut and brown butter.

name: Reblochon
description: A washed-rind cow's milk cheese from Haute-Savoie, historically made from a 'second milking' held back from tax collectors. AOP rules require animal rennet.
tasting_note: Supple and creamy with a mild nuttiness and a faint tang from its washed rind.

name: Parmigiano Reggiano
description: The classic hard, granular Italian cheese from the Parma region, aged 12-36+ months. DOP rules require calf rennet.
tasting_note: Intensely savory and nutty with crunchy tyrosine crystals and a long umami finish.

name: Pecorino Romano
description: A hard, salty sheep's milk cheese with DOP status dating back to Roman times. Traditional production uses animal (lamb) rennet.
tasting_note: Sharp, salty, and piquant — bolder and saltier than its cow's milk cousin Parmigiano.

name: Gorgonzola
description: A blue-veined cow's milk cheese named for the town near Milan where it originated. DOP rules require animal rennet.
tasting_note: Ranges from mild and creamy (dolce) to sharp and crumbly (piccante), always with a distinctive blue tang.

name: Mozzarella di Bufala Campana
description: Fresh stretched-curd cheese made from water buffalo milk in the Campania region. DOP production traditionally uses animal rennet.
tasting_note: Milky, tangy, and delicately elastic with a pool of whey released on the first bite.

name: Ricotta
description: A soft whey cheese made by re-cooking (ricotta = 're-cooked') leftover whey and coagulating it with heat and acid rather than rennet — vegetarian by process, confirmed against Cheese.com's vegetarian listing.
tasting_note: Light, slightly sweet, and grainy — a blank canvas for both savory pasta fillings and honeyed desserts.

name: Manchego
description: A firm sheep's milk cheese from the La Mancha plateau. DOP rules for traditional Manchego require animal rennet.
tasting_note: Dense and buttery with a tangy, slightly piquant bite that sharpens with age.

name: Mahón
description: A firm, rind-rubbed cow's milk cheese from Menorca. DOP production traditionally uses animal rennet.
tasting_note: Buttery and slightly salty when young, developing a sharp, piquant edge with age.

name: Requesón
description: A soft Andalusian whey cheese, similar to Italian ricotta, coagulated with heat and acid rather than rennet — no animal enzymes involved.
tasting_note: Mild, milky, and slightly sweet with a soft, spreadable curd.

name: Feta
description: Brined white cheese from Macedonia and Thrace. Marked vegetarian to reflect the commonly available microbial-rennet versions sold in most markets; some traditional/PDO producers may still use animal rennet, so check the label if buying an artisanal Greek import.
tasting_note: Tangy, salty, and crumbly with a bright, briny finish.

name: Halloumi
milk_type: sheep and goat (often blended with cow)
description: A semi-hard brined cheese famous for holding its shape when grilled or fried. Marked vegetarian to reflect the commonly available microbial-rennet versions (UK/US/EU brands); some traditional/PDO Cypriot producers may still use animal rennet, so check the label if buying traditional local batches.
tasting_note: Squeaky and salty with a milky tang; develops a golden, savory crust when seared.

name: Cheddar (vegetarian)
description: Named for the Somerset village where it originated. Per Marcella the Cheesemonger's guidance, English/UK cheddar is typically made with microbial rennet, and most supermarket cheddar is labeled vegetarian.
tasting_note: Nutty and savory when mild, sharpening to a tangy bite as it's aged.

name: Blue Stilton
description: England's famous blue cheese from Leicestershire. Blue Stilton PDO permits either animal or vegetarian rennet, but the overwhelming majority of producers use vegetarian rennet, with any animal-rennet batches clearly labeled as an exception.
tasting_note: Rich and creamy with a sharp, earthy blue tang and a lingering peppery finish.

name: Wensleydale
description: A crumbly Yorkshire cheese, traditionally paired with fruitcake. Modern commercial Wensleydale is made with microbial rennet and is widely sold as vegetarian.
tasting_note: Mild, honeyed, and slightly acidic with a moist, crumbly texture.

name: Gouda (vegetarian)
description: Named for the market town of Gouda. Many modern Dutch producers use microbial rennet for export-grade Gouda, and it is widely sold as vegetarian outside its most traditional farmhouse form.
tasting_note: Smooth and buttery when young, turning nutty and caramel-like as it's aged.

name: Edam
description: A semi-hard cheese known for its wax-coated ball shape, from the port town of Edam. Commercial production typically uses microbial rennet.
tasting_note: Mild, slightly salty, and firm with a subtle nutty sweetness.

name: Emmental
description: The classic 'holey' Swiss cheese from the Emme valley. Traditional AOP-style production uses animal rennet.
tasting_note: Mild, nutty, and slightly sweet with a springy, holey texture.

name: Gruyère
description: A firm alpine cheese from the town of Gruyères. AOP rules require traditional animal rennet.
tasting_note: Earthy and slightly sweet when young, turning deep, savory, and almost caramelized with age.

name: Havarti
description: A semi-soft Danish table cheese with small irregular holes. Danish commercial dairies commonly use microbial rennet, and it's widely sold as vegetarian.
tasting_note: Buttery and mild with a slight tang; melts smoothly.

name: Jarlsberg
description: A mild, holey Norwegian cheese resembling Emmental, developed at Jarlsberg farm near Oslo. Produced with microbial rennet and sold internationally as vegetarian.
tasting_note: Sweet and nutty with a smooth, springy bite.

name: Serra da Estrela
description: A soft, spoonable sheep's milk cheese from Portugal's highest mountains, coagulated with thistle (cardoon) flower rather than animal rennet — a hallmark of Portuguese cheesemaking per Marcella the Cheesemonger's guidance.
tasting_note: Rich, grassy, and slightly tangy with a spoonably soft, almost liquid center.

name: Bryndza
description: A soft, spreadable sheep's milk cheese central to Slovak cuisine, traditionally made with animal rennet in mountain dairies.
tasting_note: Salty, tangy, and pungent with a soft, crumbly spread.

name: Paneer
description: A fresh, non-melting cheese made by curdling hot milk with lemon juice or vinegar rather than rennet — no animal enzymes involved, a staple confirmed vegetarian across every source.
tasting_note: Mild and milky with a firm, squeaky bite that holds up well in curries and grilling.

name: Chhena
description: An unpressed, crumbly fresh cheese from West Bengal, curdled with acid and used as the base for sweets like rasgulla — no rennet used.
tasting_note: Soft, slightly sweet, and delicately crumbly.

name: Ackawi
description: A semi-soft brined cheese named for the port city of Akka (Acre), popular across the Levant. Commercial producers commonly use microbial or vegetable coagulants; noted on vegetarian-cheese checklists, though homemade/traditional batches can vary.
tasting_note: Mild and slightly salty with a smooth, sliceable texture, often studded with nigella seeds.

name: Kesong Puti
description: A fresh white Filipino cheese from Laguna province, curdled with vinegar or calamansi juice rather than rennet.
tasting_note: Soft, mildly salty, and slightly tangy with a crumbly-to-creamy texture.

name: Chhurpi
description: A hard, chewy Himalayan cheese from Nepal, Bhutan, and Tibet, traditionally made by souring and pressing skimmed milk without rennet.
tasting_note: Extremely firm and smoky, often gnawed like a chew or simmered into soups.

name: Kurt
description: Sun-dried salted balls of fermented milk curd from the Central Asian steppe, made without rennet through natural souring and pressing.
tasting_note: Intensely tangy, salty, and rock-hard — traditionally softened in the mouth or in tea.

name: Sulguni
description: A brined, pasta-filata style cheese from the Samegrelo region, traditionally coagulated with animal rennet before stretching.
tasting_note: Salty and tangy with a springy, mozzarella-like stretch.

name: Chanakh
description: A firm brined Armenian cheese aged in barrels, traditionally made with animal rennet.
tasting_note: Salty and dense with a mild tang, similar in style to Bulgarian sirene.

name: Ezine
description: A protected-origin brined white cheese from the Ezine district, traditionally made with animal rennet.
tasting_note: Rich, tangy, and slightly grassy with a firm, crumbly bite.

name: Tulum
description: A crumbly Anatolian cheese traditionally aged and pressed in goat-skin casings, made with animal rennet.
tasting_note: Sharp, salty, and pungent with a dry, crumbly texture.

name: Rushan
description: A thin, dried sheet cheese from the Bai communities of Yunnan's Dali region. Rennet source could not be confirmed against Cheese.com or Marcella the Cheesemonger's checklist, so it is marked non-vegetarian pending verification rather than assumed safe. Unknown rennet, worth checking.
tasting_note: Mild and milky, usually pan-fried or grilled until lightly crisp.

name: Byaslag
description: A dried, pressed Mongolian curd cheese made by nomadic herders. Coagulation method varies by household and could not be verified against the reference vegetarian-cheese lists, so it is marked non-vegetarian pending confirmation. Unknown rennet, worth checking.
tasting_note: Dry, dense, and mildly sour, traditionally eaten as a snack with milk tea.

name: Ayib
description: A soft, crumbly Ethiopian cottage-style cheese made by souring and straining milk — no rennet used.
tasting_note: Mild, tangy, and slightly sour, often served alongside spiced stews to cool the palate.

name: Wagashi
description: A West African cheese coagulated using the leaves and latex of the Calotropis procera plant rather than animal rennet, made by Fulani herders across Benin, Nigeria, and Togo.
tasting_note: Firm and mild, similar to paneer, and holds its shape well when grilled or fried.

name: Mish (Domiati-style)
description: A salty, fermented Egyptian cheese made by aging brined Domiati cheese in earthenware jars. Base Domiati production traditionally uses animal (calf) rennet.
tasting_note: Pungent, salty, and sharply fermented — an acquired taste often eaten with bread and onions.

name: Gibna Bayda
description: A white brined Sudanese cheese, similar to Egyptian Domiati, traditionally coagulated with animal rennet.
tasting_note: Salty and firm with a mild tang, often crumbled over legume dishes.

name: Boerenkaas
description: A Dutch-style farmhouse cheese made by South African dairies descended from Cape Dutch settler traditions. Most modern South African commercial cheesemakers use microbial rennet.
tasting_note: Buttery and mild when young, developing a firmer, nuttier bite with age.

name: Huguenot-style Fynbos Cheese
description: A Gruyère-inspired cheese from South Africa's Franschhoek wine region, made in the traditional alpine style, which typically calls for animal rennet.
tasting_note: Nutty and savory with a firm, alpine-style bite.

name: Vermont Cheddar (vegetarian)
description: Per Marcella the Cheesemonger's guidance, USA-made cheddar overwhelmingly uses microbial rennet, and most Vermont creameries label their cheddar vegetarian.
tasting_note: Clean, tangy, and grassy with a firm, crumbly bite.

name: Monterey Jack
description: A mild semi-soft cheese developed in Monterey, California. Commercial production standardly uses microbial rennet.
tasting_note: Mild, buttery, and slightly sweet, melting smoothly.

name: Colby
description: A washed-curd cheese invented in Colby, Wisconsin, softer and milder than cheddar. American commercial dairies typically use microbial rennet.
tasting_note: Mild, mellow, and slightly tangy with a springy, open texture.

name: Pepper Jack
description: Monterey Jack studded with chili peppers, a Californian favorite made with microbial rennet by most commercial producers.
tasting_note: Creamy and mild with pops of jalapeño heat and herbal spice.

name: Queso Fresco
description: A fresh, crumbly Mexican cheese, traditionally acid-set rather than rennet-coagulated — confirmed vegetarian-suitable across cheese directories.
tasting_note: Mild, milky, and slightly salty with a soft, crumbly texture.

name: Queso Oaxaca
description: A stretched-curd string cheese from Oaxaca. Commercial versions typically use microbial/vegetable rennet; traditional artisanal production may vary — check producer if strict.
tasting_note: Mild and milky with a stringy, mozzarella-like pull, popular melted in quesadillas.

name: Cotija
description: A hard, aged, crumbly cheese from Michoacán, traditionally made with animal rennet.
tasting_note: Salty and sharp, similar to a dry feta or aged Parmesan, often grated over street food.

name: Panela
description: A fresh, spongy Mexican cheese coagulated with acid rather than rennet, sold in basket-shaped molds.
tasting_note: Very mild and milky with a firm, slightly springy bite that holds up to grilling.

name: Oka
description: A semi-soft washed-rind cheese developed by Trappist monks in Oka, Quebec, made with animal rennet following monastic tradition.
tasting_note: Earthy and nutty with a pungent, washed-rind aroma and a supple, melting interior.

name: Cream Cheese (Philadelphia-style)
description: A fresh, spreadable American cheese typically set with lactic acid cultures and little to no rennet; most commercial brands are labeled vegetarian.
tasting_note: Rich, tangy, and smooth with a thick, spreadable texture.

name: Queijo Minas Frescal
description: A fresh white cheese from Minas Gerais, coagulated primarily with acid and light heat rather than rennet.
tasting_note: Mild, milky, and slightly salty with a soft, moist curd.

name: Queijo Coalho
description: A firm, grillable cheese from Brazil's northeast whose name literally means 'rennet cheese.' Whether producers commonly use animal or microbial rennet could not be confirmed against the reference vegetarian lists, so it is marked non-vegetarian pending verification. Unknown rennet, worth checking.
tasting_note: Salty and squeaky, famous for being skewered and grilled over open coals at the beach.

name: Queso Blanco
description: A fresh acid-set cheese common across Colombia and Venezuela, made without rennet by curdling milk with vinegar or lime juice.
tasting_note: Mild and milky with a firm, squeaky bite, often fried until golden.

name: Queso Paraguayo
description: A soft, mild fresh cheese used in Paraguay's chipa bread. Coagulation method varies by producer and could not be confirmed against reference lists, so it is marked non-vegetarian pending verification. Unknown rennet, worth checking.
tasting_note: Mild, milky, and slightly salty, prized for melting smoothly into baked goods.

name: Reggianito
description: An Argentine hard grating cheese developed by Italian immigrants in imitation of Parmigiano Reggiano, traditionally made with animal rennet.
tasting_note: Sharp and savory, milder and moister than true Parmigiano but similarly grate-friendly.

name: Requesón Andino
description: An Andean whey cheese similar to ricotta, made by re-cooking whey with acid — no rennet involved.
tasting_note: Soft, mild, and slightly sweet, often eaten with corn or in stuffed peppers.

name: Pyengana Cheddar
description: A clothbound farmhouse cheddar from Pyengana, Tasmania. Its exact rennet source is not clearly documented on Cheese.com or Marcella the Cheesemonger's checklist, so it is marked non-vegetarian pending confirmation from the producer. Unknown rennet, worth checking.
tasting_note: Sharp, tangy, and slightly crumbly with a distinctive farmhouse funk.

name: King Island Cheddar
description: A rich cheddar from King Island's grass-fed dairy herds. Like most modern Australian commercial cheddar, it is made with microbial rennet.
tasting_note: Creamy and rich with a clean, buttery tang from the island's grass-fed milk.

name: Kapiti Kikorangi Blue
description: A creamy New Zealand blue cheese from the Kapiti Coast. Rennet source was not confirmed against the reference vegetarian-cheese lists, so it is marked non-vegetarian pending verification. Unknown rennet, worth checking.
tasting_note: Rich and creamy with a mellow, mildly spicy blue tang.

name: Mercer Colby
description: A mild Colby-style cheese from the Waikato dairy region. New Zealand commercial cheesemakers commonly use microbial rennet, similar to UK/USA practice.
tasting_note: Mild, buttery, and smooth with a springy, open texture.

name: Whitestone Windsor Blue
description: An award-winning blue cheese from Oamaru's Whitestone Cheese. Rennet source could not be confirmed against the reference vegetarian-cheese lists, so it is marked non-vegetarian pending confirmation. Unknown rennet, worth checking.
tasting_note: Creamy and mellow with a gentle blue tang and a smooth, dense paste.

name: Meredith Dairy Marinated Goat Cheese
description: A fresh marinated chèvre-style cheese from Victoria's Meredith Dairy. Fresh chèvre production commonly uses microbial rennet, and the product is labeled vegetarian-suitable.
tasting_note: Tangy and creamy, steeped in herbed olive oil with a soft, spoonable texture.
